```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The sample sheet (`pheno` in `qc_config()`) is optional, but it is what lets
prepDNAm check the samples against what you expect: reported sex against the
sex predicted from the data, chronological against epigenetic age, and which
samples should come from the same person. This guide describes the format.

# File format

A `.csv`, `.tsv`/`.txt`, `.xlsx`, `.rds` or `.Rdata` file, or a data frame, with
one row per sample and a header row. Column names are case-sensitive.

```
basename,sex,age,donor_id,group
206467010001_R01C01,F,34.5,D001,control
206467010001_R02C01,M,51,D002,case
206467010001_R03C01,F,,D001,control
206467010001_R04C01,unknown,62,D003,case
```

# Standard columns

| Column | Required | Format | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `basename` | yes | sample name exactly as in the data | matching rows to samples |
| `sex` | no | `F` / `M` | sex check (report page 5), `Sex` in the CSV export |
| `age` | no | number, in years | epigenetic vs chronological age (page 5), `Age` in the CSV export |
| `donor_id` | no | any text | genotype identity check (page 5), SNP pair plots |
| `batch` | no | any text | default batching |
| `exclude` | no | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | samples to drop from the start |

All other columns are kept: they appear in the samples table, are carried into
`pheno_postQC.rds` and the export, and are tested against the principal
components on the PCA page (useful to spot batch effects, e.g. by plate or
collection date).

## `basename`

The sample identifier as it appears in the data:

- **IDATs:** the file name without `_Grn.idat` / `_Red.idat` (and without
  `.gz`), usually `<Sentrix ID>_<position>`, e.g. `206467010001_R01C01` for
  `206467010001_R01C01_Grn.idat`. Not the path, just the name.
- **Signal-intensity matrix:** the column name without the suffix, e.g.
  `GSM1234567` for `GSM1234567 Methylated signal`.
- **Beta matrix:** the column name.

Matching is exact. Every `basename` in the sample sheet must be found in the
data (otherwise the run stops and lists the missing ones); samples in the data
but not in the sample sheet are dropped with a message, so the sample sheet
can be used to select a subset. Values must be unique and not empty. A column
called `Basename` (any capitalisation) is accepted.

## `sex`

Reported sex, as `F` or `M`. `female` / `male` in any capitalisation are also
accepted. If not known, leave the cell empty or write `NA` or `unknown`.

Numeric codes (`0`/`1`, `1`/`2`) are **not** accepted: conventions differ
between cohorts and a silent mix-up would flag every sample as a mismatch or
hide real ones. Recode them to `F`/`M` first, e.g.

```{r}
pheno$sex <- c(`1` = "M", `2` = "F")[as.character(pheno$sex_code)]
```

Predicted sex (from the chrX and chrY probe intensities) is compared with this
column and mismatches are listed in the report. A mismatch usually means a
sample swap or a sample sheet error, and occasionally a sex chromosome
aneuploidy.

## `age`

Chronological age at sampling, in years, as a plain number. Decimals are fine
(`34.5`, `0.5` for six months). No units (`45y`), ranges (`40-50`) or text.
Leave empty or `NA` if not known. Ages above 120 give a warning, since they
usually mean the wrong unit (e.g. months).

## `donor_id`

An identifier for the person each sample comes from. Samples from the same
person (technical replicates, repeated samples over time, different tissues)
share a `donor_id`; everyone else has a different one. Any text works (a study
ID, a pseudonym); it does not need to be meaningful outside the sample sheet.

The array's SNP probes give each sample a genotype fingerprint. With
`donor_id`, the report lists samples whose genotype disagrees with their
donor's other samples (a mislabelled or swapped sample) or matches a
different donor's (a duplicate or swap). Without it, the report still shows
which samples appear to come from the same person. This needs IDAT input and
the `ewastools` package.

## `batch` and `exclude`

- `batch`: used as the batching mode when `qc_config(batch = NULL)`, e.g. the
  processing plate. Any other column can be chosen with `batch = "<column>"`.
- `exclude`: `TRUE`, `yes` or `1` marks samples to remove before
  normalisation (e.g. known failed samples). They are still read and shown in
  the report with the reason `excluded`. Excluded samples can also be given
  with `qc_config(exclude = )` as a vector or file of basenames.

# Checks when the run starts

When the run is initialised, prepDNAm checks the sample sheet and stops with a
message listing the affected samples if:

- `basename` is missing, has empty or duplicated values, or names samples not
  found in the data;
- `sex` has values other than F/M (or the accepted spellings and unknowns);
- `age` has values that are not numbers, or negative ages.

An `age` column stored as text (common in Excel files) is converted to
numbers.

# Other column names

If your sample sheet uses other names, prepDNAm recognises common
alternatives and says which column it uses:

| Standard | Also recognised |
|---|---|
| `sex` | `gender`, `reported_sex` |
| `age` | `age_at_sampling`, `chron_age`, `chronological_age` |
| `donor_id` | `donor`, `person`, `person_id`, `individual`, `subject`, `patient`, `participant` |

Renaming to the standard names is recommended. For any other name, pass it
explicitly:

```{r}
qc_report("runs/study1", sex_col = "Sex_reported", donor_col = "PatientNo")
export_beta_csv("runs/study1", sex_col = "Sex_reported", age_col = "AgeYears")
```

# GEO data

For GEO series, the sample names in the data are usually the GSM accessions,
so use them as `basename`. Sex and age are typically in the
`characteristics_ch1` fields of the series matrix, in study-specific wording
(`gender: female`, `age (years): 45`); extract them into `sex` and `age`
columns in the format above. When exporting for sharing, `export_beta_csv()`
uses `basename` as `SampleID`; pass `sample_id = "<column>"` to use another
column.
